key_insight: A coupled CEL simulation and ANN surrogate model can accurately predict friction stir welding quality in HDPE and identify process windows that minimize defects.
engineering_relevance: This work provides practical guidance for selecting rotation speed, traverse speed, and preheating to stabilize force/temperature responses and improve weld integrity in thermoplastics.
method: 3D Coupled Eulerian-Lagrangian (CEL) model for thermal-mechanical FSW physics
Two multilayer perceptron ANNs trained on experimental time-series temperature and axial-force data
Process map generation to classify defect-free and defective welding conditions
evidence_signal: The ANN models achieved R2 values between 0.91 and 0.99, and the CEL predictions matched experiments for void formation, thermal response, and force trends.
watch_item: The model is validated on the tested HDPE parameter space, so performance and optimal settings may not transfer directly to other polymers, tool geometries, or broader operating ranges.
paper_title: Computational and machine learning modelling approaches for weld quality predictions in friction stir welding of high-density polyethylene
